meta.note: First real backtest, run in the build sandbox on 2026-10-09. Journals 2025-040 (3,434 records) and 2025-041 (3,749 records) were downloaded from ipo.gov.uk with `backtest ingest --source ukipo_http` (2025-040 is the earliest journal the probe found still served; see availability.json). This environment has no Companies House bulk index and no API key, so no applicant could be matched to a company: every brand is scored as unmatched, and all 152 land in SUPPRESS on both the stored and the point-in-time score. No web search (never used by a backtest), no domain layer, and no rescan has run, so there is not one outcome observation: every label is 'unknown' (no evidence). This report proves the path end to end and measures nothing. Re-run it after a full ingest with the Companies House index available, and again as rescans accumulate observations inside the +3/+6 month windows.
caveats: Labels come only from observations already stored, observed on or before the horizon end (positive) or within the tolerance after it (negative). Brands ingested from past journals have no observations from their horizon windows, so they stay 'unknown' until rescans that fall inside a window accumulate.
'Launched' includes brands that were already trading at filing: no point-in-time record of a pre-filing website exists, so the label cannot tell 'launched after filing' from 'already launched'.
Survivorship: only filings that reached the opportunity stage get brands; rejected records are not in the population.
The PIT score excludes web, current Companies House and live-site inputs, so it is lower and flatter than a live score (it is capped below HIGH, as any score without web evidence is).
'First trade mark for this applicant' is judged against the journals in the database only; the oldest ingested journal sees every applicant as new.
The major-brand-owner list and the product taxonomy are today's configuration.
